texts.text:
A monarchy in the northern reaches of the Continent of Atlasia, founded a millennium ago by the Elysians who migrated northward during the Great Migration. The name Hyperborea means "the land of the far north."

In the year 20 of the New Calendar, Dis Galea was crowned as Dis Ⅰ at Icelake Keep, marking the formal establishment of the Hyperborean Empire. In the year 47, Empress Bellona Ⅰ relocated the capital to Dismania.

The Empire's history is one of conquest. Through mastery of Phoxichor and alchemical technology, Hyperborea enforces its rule by military might. It remains in long-standing conflict with the Elysian Church, whose people worship the Great Nine.

The current emperor of Hyperborean Empire is Julius.

A resistance group active within the Hyperborean Empire, composed primarily of Charons disillusioned with imperial rule. Through various extreme methods, they seek to influence policy — and in some cases, to overthrow the Empire entirely. In recent years, the group has been linked to numerous armed clashes and assassinations across imperial territory.

Some members of The Forsakens possess the ability to manipulate Filthoids through specific sound-based techniques, provoking heightened aggression and using them as living weapons against their enemies.

Within the organisation, members are ranked across four descending tiers of authority: Messenger, Longmane, Raven, and Wildswarm.
Above them all stands the Hazering — a conclave of seven Messengers, revered as the supreme authority of the Forsakens.

The Empire's primary military force, comprising 13 legions, each tasked with a distinct role.

The 13th Legion, led by Sibylle, answers directly to the Emperor and is responsible for special operations assigned by him — most notably those involving the Forsakens.
The military force responsible for maintaining public order and security in Icelake. Operates under the command of the Empire's 6th Legion.

While officially tasked with protecting all citizens of Icelake, the Escort often focuses disproportionately on matters concerning the Solarian community. Certain personnel within the unit have even been known to abuse their authority, openly mistreating Charon civilians under the pretext of maintaining order.

An official academic institution of the Hyperborean Empire.

Alchemists in Hyperborea were once akin to their counterparts across the continent — enigmatic figures detached from everyday life. This began to change under Queen Bellona Ⅱ, who founded the Royal Alchemy Academy and gradually redefined the role of alchemists within the Empire.

Originally a small scholarly organisation, the Academy gathered the Empire's brightest minds under royal patronage to pursue legendary goals, such as elemental transmutation for military use. Though such ambitions were never realised, centuries of research eventually led to the discovery of Phoxichor — an energy source as precious as gold, refined from Phoxene. This breakthrough marked the dawn of Phoxene technology and elevated alchemists to the forefront of national development. Over time, alchemists became synonymous with Imperial scholars, employed by the state to advance its industry, infrastructure, and military arsenal through Phoxene-tech applications. The Academy itself has since evolved into a vast network of research branches across the Empire's major cities.

Today, the Academy is divided into two principal branches: The Aeolipile and The Spathatoi. The Aeolipile — also known as the Old Academy — continues the institution's original mission, focusing on mechanical invention, engineering projects, and weapons development powered by Phoxene-based technologies. By contrast, The Spathatoi, or New Academy, was founded by Emperor Julius I with support from the 13th Legion. It absorbed the Academy's former biological sciences and now leads research into life sciences, medicine, and Charon magic.

The Hyperborean Military Council serves as the Empire's central administrative authority. Its members are appointed directly by the emperor and are tasked with assisting in matters of state governance. Unlike the aristocrat-dominated Senate, the Military Council includes individuals of humble origin, elevated through merit and exceptional ability.

A theocratic state in the southern reaches of the Continent of Atlasia, centred around a sacred tower where, according to legend, nine deities once revealed themselves. Regarded as the oldest of all human civilisations, Elysium follows the Elysian Orthodox Faith, which venerates the Great Nine. All civil affairs are governed by the Elysian Church, which interprets divine will.

The faith promotes ideals of fairness and shared joy, fostering millennia of peaceful coexistence among the diverse races under its rule.

As the Nine Chapters of Dafeng grew increasingly rigid, many injustices went unanswered. In response, a band of outlaws emerged, defying the law by force and dispensing justice in their own way. They are known as the Drifters.
Although the reform of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng has formally lifted the warrants against the Drifters, public fear and prejudice towards them are unlikely to fade any time soon.

A Phoxhunter team formed by {nickname}, Outsider, and Snow.

While Outsider and Snow proposed naming the group "Intern Researchers on the 99 Innovative Culinary Styles of Delicious Winged Hexapods of the Demon King of Ultralight from the Pure White Infernal," {nickname} ultimately drew inspiration from the words of the mysterious figure in {性别:his|her} dream and chose Noctoyagers instead — a name simple in form, yet quietly resonant in meaning.

A nation lying to the south of the Hyperborean Empire, bordered by the Elysian Church to the south and Hyperborea to the north. It was founded a millennium ago by Alexis, one of the leaders of the Great Migration.

Nestled among mountains and forests, Aethyrie maintains a policy of permanent neutrality. Its people are devoted to the pursuit of knowledge, rarely involving themselves in conflicts beyond their borders. Yet its unique location ensures that such conflicts are never far away.

A reticent girl of few words, untainted by the ways of the world. She lives with {nickname} in a village on Purgatorio Island. The two have depended on one another since childhood, regarding each other as family closer than blood.
Referred to by the Hyperborean military as "No. 0," she has long been the subject of an ongoing manhunt. Following a confrontation with Sibylle, her current whereabouts are unknown.
Sibylle Mason, chief of the Hyperborean Empire's 13th Legion. She appeared on Purgatorio Island in pursuit of Berenica, whom she refers to as "No. 0."
Randy Howard is an officer of the Hyperborean Empire's 13th Legion, currently serving as adjutant to Chief Sibylle.

Camilla Scarlet, proprietress of The Asphodel, a well-known tavern in Icelake. Smooth and well-connected.

She was entrusted by a mysterious white-clad figure to rescue the wandering {nickname} and assist with {性别:his|her} temporary stay in Icelake.
A Lunarian who, together with Camilla, rescued {nickname}. Recognisable by a pair of demon-like horns resembling those of the Charon, she speaks in an exaggerated, theatrical manner.

She refers to herself as the "Pure-White Redeemer ☆ Demon King of Light!" Though she doesn't appear to crave human praise like most Lunarians, her behaviour otherwise mirrors theirs in nearly every way.
Henrik Ethelred, proprietor of the inn known as Hypnos' House. A distant and taciturn man, he is known for his deep distrust of strangers.

Once a renowned physician in Icelake, Henrik was celebrated for his exceptional skill — his patients even included nobles from the inner city. After the early death of his wife, he raised their only daughter, Hayley, on his own.
Several years ago, during a journey to Scarletriver, he was arrested and imprisoned for murder. As the victim was a Charon exhibiting signs of Deterioration, Henrik served only a brief sentence before being released. He returned to Icelake alone. Hayley was never seen again.

The Charon citizen Henrik killed was, in truth, his own daughter. When Hayley began to show early signs of Deterioration, Henrik took her to Scarletriver in search of a cure and began researching a suppressant. But the affliction advanced before his work could be completed.
To spare her the fate of becoming a Filthoid, Henrik ended her life with his own hands — allowing his daughter to depart with the dignity of a human.
Psyche Frey, a cheerful and bright-spirited girl who serves as both lodger and attendant at Hypnos' House.
Psyche had a deep love for tending flowers and plants. However, due to illness, her vision gradually deteriorated, and she eventually lost her sight.

At the age of seventeen, after exhibiting early signs of Deterioration, Psyche was left with no other choice but to part from her birth parents and seek refuge at Hypnos' House.

As her condition worsened, she volunteered to undergo Henrik's experimental Deterioration suppressant — clinging to a slim hope of survival. But the treatment failed. The drug accelerated the progression of her symptoms, and she ultimately transformed into a Filthoid.

Outside Icelake, she encountered {nickname}. Stirred by {nickname}'s words, she briefly regained a flicker of awareness and remembered who she was. Unwilling to live as a monster, she chose to end her life.

A bright and spirited scavenger girl from Icelake. Kind-hearted and full of warmth, she always shares her finds with those in need around her. The people of the slums fondly call her "Princess Rubbish Bin."

{nickname}'s journey as a Phoxhunter began with her — a task to recover her stolen purse.

A nimble Phoxhunter based in Icelake, free-spirited and quick-witted, with a tendency to run his mouth. He first crossed paths with {nickname} while pursuing a commission involving the rare mineral Crystallo of Stella.

A Charon girl of delicate health and the younger sister of Outsider. Lives in near-seclusion.

Obsessed with fairy tales, Fina speaks and acts as though she herself were a character from one — sweet, innocent, dreamy, and a little lost in wonder.

Inspired by her encounter with {nickname}, Fina began to yearn for the world beyond her home. Encouraged by Outsider, she bravely stepped out, made many new friends, and unexpectedly reunited with her only living relative, Savio.
Her love for fairy tales has granted her the power to summon storybook friends, bringing her vibrant imagination to life and arming her with the bravery to confront any peril.
Rhythm Fischer, a warrant officer of the Escort under the 6th Legion. Known for her diligence and discipline, she prioritises the safety of civilians above all else.
Born in Mist Aken and raised in hardship, Rhythm developed a deep empathy for underprivileged Charon citizens. Even beyond her official duties, she often went out of her way to offer them support.
Rhythm once took part in the 6th Legion's entrance trials alongside her younger brother, Blues. Although she did not pass, she later joined the Icelake Escort.

During her childhood, Rhythm's parents were killed after unknowingly sheltering a Deteriorator — an act that led to severe civilian casualties. Since then, she has vowed never to let anyone fall victim to a Filthoid again.
In truth, it was Rhythm herself who had urged her parents to take in the Deteriorator. She has borne the weight of guilt ever since.

Recognised for her outstanding actions during the Charon Hunt investigation, Rhythm was awarded the title of Laurelled Charon. However, having lost both a loved one and her sense of purpose, she eventually resigned from her post in the Escort.

Rhythm travelled to Dismania to help {nickname} search for their missing family. However, the information she uncovered inadvertently led {nickname} into a train hijacking, after which they disappeared. When news of their disappearance reached Rhythm, she had no choice but to return to Icelake.
While going through Blues's belongings at their hideout, Rhythm found an old list of recruits accepted into the 6th Legion. The names on it led her to seek out the families of those who had fallen victim to the Legion's experiments. Along the way, she met people from many different walks of life — and eventually Rae, a young woman who, like Rhythm, had lost someone she loved to the Legion. Rhythm stopped Rae before she could carry out a desperate act of revenge. In Rae, she saw a reflection of her own grief and self-destructive guilt. The encounter made Rhythm realise that continuing to punish herself would change nothing. She chose instead to move forward with her life and find a new purpose.

Daphne Theodore, a field medic of the 13th Legion, quiet and mild-mannered in disposition. Exceptionally bright and diligent, she once studied under the chief alchemist at the Alchemy Academy of Hyperborea and was widely considered a rising star in the field. Motivated by personal conviction, she eventually left the Academy to serve as a medic in the Legion, where she became a trusted comrade of {nickname2}.

The daughter of Avar. Though he never spoke of the reasons behind his absence, Daphne's perceptiveness allowed her to understand the truth on her own. Grateful for his silent love and sacrifice, she has come to believe she must forge her own path — not as a child shielded by those who care for her, but as an equal, facing the world alongside them.

Avar Hrodland, captain of the 13th Legion's Snow Wolves squad and former instructor to {nickname2} during {性别2:his|her} time at the Imperial Military College. A seasoned and dependable soldier, respected both as a mentor and a comrade.

Avar is the biological father of Daphne. Years ago, when Emperor Julius shifted the Empire's policy towards Charon citizens from leniency to suppression, Daphne's mother chose to divorce Avar and legally changed their daughter's surname to safeguard her future.

Avar agreed to the arrangement and, to prevent young Daphne from clinging to the past, deliberately maintained the facade of an absent and indifferent father. Even after reuniting with her in the legion, he preserved a strict emotional distance to conceal their true relationship.
During the Lonza Fortress Operation, Avar uncovered Fulvis' conspiracy and was killed by Fulvis in an attempt to silence him.

In a final effort to ensure the truth behind the Lonza incident would not be buried, Avar devised a plan before his death. He faked the execution of {nickname2} and pledged loyalty to Fulvis, using the deception to secure {nickname2}'s escape. In doing so, he sacrificed his life and left behind an audio recording as vital evidence.

Months ago, Avar wandered into Mount Arcano and, under the influence of drugs, played the role of "The Devil" Aamon for several days. Eventually, he regained his senses, uncovered the secret of the Catalyst, and escaped Mount Arcano. On his deathbed during the Battle of Lonza Fortress, he entrusted this secret to {nickname2}.

Antonius Fulvis, colonel of the 13th Legion and commanding officer of the Lonza Fortress Operation.

A scion of an old Hyperborean noble house, Fulvis rose to his position in the military through hereditary influence in the Senate rather than combat merit. Arrogant and self-assured, he is known for making rash strategic decisions with little regard for the safety of his subordinates.

A hardline extremist among the Solarian, Fulvis harbours a deep-seated hatred towards the Charon. He regards Emperor Julius' early conciliatory policies towards the Charon community as signs of weakness and holds Chief Sibylle in thinly veiled contempt, quietly coveting her position in the Legion.

During the Lonza Fortress Operation, Fulvis deliberately leaked classified intelligence to The Forsakens, then fabricated evidence to frame Avar — a Charon officer — for treason. His ultimate goal was to instigate a purge of Charon personnel from the Empire's upper military ranks.
Fulvis infiltrated Mount Arcano alone for the complete Catalyst, while his soldiers were stationed nearby and did not follow him in.

Fulvis lost his memories of the past and played the role of "The Fool" Joy, Victor's friend, in Paradise Village. To help {nickname2} escape, he threw himself in front of the village chief's gun and was shot dead.

Fulvis did not lose his memory. He had been posing as "The Fool" Joy all along, quietly stoking conflict between {nickname2} and Paradise Village, waiting for both sides to exhaust each other so he could seize the Catalyst.

{nickname2} saw through Fulvis's disguise and swapped out Fulvis's communicator well in advance, thwarting his scheme. Realising there was no way out, Fulvis detonated his combat vehicle and set Arcano ablaze in an attempt to take {nickname2} and the others down with him.

A young Charon lady captured by the Griffins during the Lonza Fortress Operation. She claims not to be a member of The Forsakens, insisting she was a civilian conscripted by the group to assist with mechanical modifications at the fortress.

Full name: Katya Oen. Formerly a civilian, she was forcibly requisitioned by the Empire to perform maintenance duties at Lonza Fortress. She later defected to The Forsakens, who had rescued her during their occupation of the fortress. Katya participated in The Forsakens' assault on the Hyperborean Legion, but deliberately stayed behind when the others retreated — surrendering herself in order to meet {nickname2}, also known as the Pale Reaper. Her motives remain unclear.

Reappears in Chapter Noctoyager. In Icelake, she set an elaborate plan in motion, ordering one of her subordinates to plant bombs in Bloomfield Station. This forced the station's security to focus on protecting the Jackdaw, leaving the ordinary trains lightly guarded and allowing her to hijack one of them.
She currently serves as the Beast-King of the Hazering within the Forsakens. Her apparent objective in hijacking the train was to set a Heaventree ablaze, though her true motives remain unknown.
A soldier of the Hyperborean Empire's 13th Legion, serving as adjutant to Colonel Fulvis.

Falsi took possession of Avar's audio recording — a key piece of evidence in the Lonza treason case. During the explosion at the fortress, she was separated from her unit and has not been seen since. The recording was lost in the incident, and its current whereabouts remain unknown.
Falsi survived the explosion at Lonza Fortress. She claims that Avar's recording was destroyed in the blast.
Falsi was a classmate of {nickname2} at the Imperial Military College and briefly fought alongside {性别2：him|her}.

After surviving Lonza Fortress, Falsi's only reason to live was to kill Fulvis and then take her own life.
After destroying Arcano alongside {nickname2} and foiling Fulvis's schemes, Falsi found a new purpose: to confront every crime she had committed.
To that end, she walked alone into the flames to find the recording that held the truth of Lonza Fortress — taking her first step toward atonement.

A prominent noble of Hyperborea and a former leading member of the Military Council. He served as regent during the early years of Emperor Julius's reign, assisting the young sovereign in quelling the Charon Uprising and introducing reforms aimed at improving the rights and status of the Charon people — efforts that greatly eased ethnic tensions within the Empire.

The current emperor of the Hyperborean Empire. He ascended the throne at a young age and, with the support of Duke Servius, initially introduced a series of reforms aimed at alleviating the oppression and marginalisation of the Charon community, in an effort to ease domestic tensions. For reasons unknown, these conciliatory policies were later abandoned in favour of a more repressive stance.

Hellfire Surt currently serves as the Warden of the Hyperborean Imperial Military Prison.

A direct descendant of the Surt bloodline, she exhibits the family's distinctive traits: skin of vivid, flame-like red and a body temperature so high that few can approach her without being burned.

Fiercely devoted to justice and order, she maintains an uncompromising stance against deceit and the concealment of truth.

The Warden's weapon, Inferno, is a unique artefact passed down exclusively through the Surt lineage. Its extreme heat and power are said to be unbearable for any bearer outside the family, making the position of Warden effectively hereditary since the post's inception.

During the Lonza treason case, Hellfire conducted a drug-induced hypnotic interrogation of {nickname2}. Convinced of the authenticity of {性别2:his|her} testimony, she authorised a deeper investigation into the matter.
A prince of the Hyperborean Empire and younger brother to Emperor Julius.

Despite his noble birth, Vergilius is known for his gentle disposition and informal manners. He is an old acquaintance of {nickname2}.

During the investigation into the Lonza treason case, Vergilius intervened with a royal pardon signed by the emperor, successfully securing the release of both {nickname2} and Daphne before their scheduled execution.
Originally named Dis Galea, he rose to prominence as a distinguished commander during the Great Migration and later became the founding sovereign of the Galea dynasty in Hyperborea.

As imperial records attest, in the turbulent years following the Night of Lamenting Lake, Dis Ⅰ led the Solarian in rising against the Charon's atrocities. Yet in the wake of securing victory, he chose not vengeance, but forgiveness — and so began the great era known as the Silver Peace.

The current director of the Magic Flute Troupe. Now in her later years, she remains meticulous and unwavering in her oversight, managing every detail with exceptional care. Thanks to her consistent efforts, the troupe has maintained a high standard of performance for over a decade and is widely recognised in Icelake for its excellence.

The leading soprano of the Magic Flute Troupe and one of Hyperborea's most celebrated opera performers, renowned for her masterful vocal expression and transformative stagecraft. Her remarkable ability to shift both voice and appearance with ease has earned her the nickname "Violetta of a Hundred Faces."

Her real name is Enola Ruthford, daughter of Fabrice Ruthford, the officer once in charge of Glevum Pit.
A kidnapping first brought her into contact with Violet, a girl of humble origins who dreamed of becoming a playwright. After Violet's death, Enola faked her own, assumed the name Violetta with the help of Violet's elder brother, Sig, and fled to Luca to study opera.
Now a celebrated singer, Violetta returns home to bring Putini — the opera she co-wrote with her late friend — to the local stage. She dedicates herself to training young opera talent, regardless of birth or status.
If Phoxhunter rumours are to be believed, she has also been quietly searching for a missing student known as Parsifal.

Blues Fischer, a young Charon born and raised in Icelake, is the younger brother of Rhythm Fischer. Aspiring to become a Laurelled Charon, he enlisted in the 6th Legion and successfully passed its selection process, later enrolling in a three-year closed training programme.

After joining the 6th Legion, Blues was forcibly subjected to alchemical modification by the Spathatoi, resulting in the loss of his human body. He was transformed into a being of exceptional combat prowess. Following his escape from the facility, the effects of an experimental suppressant led to a steady deterioration of his condition. As he gradually lost control, he began launching a series of nocturnal attacks on civilians — later identified as the true origin of the Charon Hunt in Icelake. During a confrontation with Rhythm, he sustained fatal injuries. To spare his sister the burden of knowing the truth, he asked a friend to conceal the real cause of his death.
A major of the Hyperborean Empire's 13th Legion. Lynn is a no-nonsense officer assigned to Icelake to oversee the investigation into the Charon Hunt case.

Another test subject from the 6th Legion's augmentation programme. Phantasio met Blues during their confinement at the facility. The two became friends and later escaped together. He was later identified as the figure behind the latter stages of the Charon Hunt. In order to honour Blues' final wish, Phantasio damaged his own vocal cords to impersonate him, and revealed the truth to Rhythm.

Real name: Parsifal Snowfield. He once starred as the frost fairy in the final performance of Children From the Snowfield.

At the conclusion of the Charon Hunt investigation, he knocked Rhythm unconscious and entrusted her to {nickname}. To conceal {nickname}'s in the skirmish with the 13th Legion, Phantasio remained behind to cover their retreat and erase all traces. During the ensuing clash with Lynn's unit, he was critically wounded and taken into custody by the 13th Legion. His current whereabouts remain unknown.

A noble from the inner city of Icelake, carries herself with pride but possesses a inherently good nature.
She came to the surrounding districts to aid her friend Savio, where she met Fina and {nickname}. After a kidnapping incident, she overcame her prejudice against the Charons and formed a firm friendship with Fina.

A youth from the inner city, Fina's half-brother.
After losing both parents, he suffered bullying at school. Believing his only friend Cassandra had abandoned him, he fled Icelake alone, only to be kidnapped by bandits.
He was safely rescued by Fina and {nickname}, leading to his reunion with Fina. Encouraged by {nickname}, he has found the courage to face life anew.

A thief who came to Huaxu from overseas. Calling herself the "Demon Tabethe the Red Hand", she claims to steal only from baddies and never target good people. Skilled in disguise and shapeshifting, she also seems to have a soft spot for sea creatures. She carries out her thefts by summoning strange tentacles. Her mimicry is so flawless that she can even elude the punishments of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.
The stationmaster of Icelake Station. A highly capable man said to keep the entire station in impeccable order. Best not to get on his bad side.

The stationmaster of Bloomfield Station. A shrewd and highly capable man with a firm grip on everything that happens there. He once took Outsider hostage to force the Noctoyagers to assist in the investigation of a bombing at the station, while also providing them with considerable support throughout the case.

A former Imperial soldier, he later joined Bloomfield Station, rose steadily through the ranks, and ultimately turned it into a kingdom of his own.

A mysterious woman who appeared on the roof of one of the Jackdaw's carriages. She claims to be nothing more than a maid, yet possesses exceptional combat skill. So far, she has shown no clear hostility.

The personal attendant of Princess Flora of the Hyperborean Empire. Highly skilled in disguise, she fled Dismania alongside Flora and now presents herself simply as "Flora's maid".

After Flora was imprisoned once again through the schemes of the veteran agent known as "Concerto", Hilda returned to her side. She is now secretly seeking a way to help Flora escape once more.

A member of the Forsakens who holds the rank of Raven. By luring Carnot with the promise of two tickets to Dismania, Halogi secured his help in planting bombs throughout Bloomfield Station as part of a threat against the Empire.

Full name: Flodia Proserpina Galea. The daughter of Hyperborea's previous emperor and the niece of the current one, she spent many years under house arrest in the Imperial Palace as a suspected claimant to the throne.

After escaping the Imperial Capital with Hilda's help under the alias "Flora", she fell into the hands of the 13th Legion. She is now set to be taken back to Dismania aboard Sibylle Mason's private train, the Jackdaw.
According to the villagers of Arcano, {nickname2}'s real name is Victor, who left the hometown of Arcano four years ago to join the Legion.
{nickname2} is not Victor. Everything is a lie fabricated by the villagers of Arcano. The real Victor was a resident of Arcano who died in the war four years ago.
One of the villagers of Arcano. She appears simple-minded with a slightly scattered way of thinking. According to her, she is Victor's childhood friend.
Falsi witnessed Ada coldly killing other villagers. Ada seems far less innocent than she appears.
During Mother Bunny's trial, Ada abandoned the name "Ada" given to her by Mother Bunny and chose a new name for herself: "Eve".

She is actually a replica created by Mother Bunny — the real Ada — modelled after herself. During the crisis in Arcano, without anyone knowing, Eve inherited Ada's replication ability. She bid farewell to {nickname2} and set out to see the world beyond Mount Arcano on Ada's behalf.
The true master of the town of Arcano, who usually only appears during the Parade. All residents of Arcano are Mother Bunny's "little bunnies."

Mother Bunny is a mysterious and powerful Daimon, and the bearer of the key Catalyst for the "Second Scion Program." According to Avar's intel, no matter what happens — even if it means taking the Catalyst and her enemies down with her — she will never hand it over.

Mother Bunny is the real Ada, the sole survivor of Arcano from four years ago. The current "High Priestess" Ada is a replica created by Mother Bunny in her own image, playing the role of Ada in Paradise Village.
Ada used her last strength to help {nickname2} and the others escape the burning ruins of the town of Arcano, then walked into the flames with the village chief, vanishing from sight.

Rae Sloan is the younger sister of Darcy Sloan, one of the victims of the 6th Legion's clandestine experiments. Rae possesses a rare magical ability that allows her to glimpse fragments of her sister's memories in dreams. Through those dreams, she uncovered part of the truth surrounding Darcy's death. Consumed by grief and rage, Rae sought revenge against the Legion, setting her sights on Lieutenant Colonel Johnson, who had been responsible for maintaining order at the recruitment site. She began plotting to assassinate him.
Rhythm uncovered the plot by chance and intervened before Rae could carry it out. With Rhythm's help, Rae eventually gave up her plans for revenge and chose instead to move forward with her life, carrying the memories of her sister with her.
A mysterious merchant from Huaxu who holds a high position despite being a Charon. She first met {nickname} after intervening to help at Galea Theatre.
During a Legion operation designed to lure out {nickname}, Zhiliu intervened once more, rescuing and escorting {nickname} to Huaxu.

As the High Chancellor of Loongyuan, Zhiliu leads the Ministry of Fortune and chairs the merchant guild, EverSpring. Preferring the title of merchant, she is known for her approachable demeanor and sharp business acumen, earning her wide respect among Starweavers.

Zhiliu seeks to resolve the Scourge of Zhuyin. To this end, she has commissioned {nickname} to harvest Zhuyin Scales.
A highly concentrated reactive substance that resonates with these scales was what originally drew her to Icelake. While her initial objective there failed, it led to her unexpected discovery of {nickname}.
Zhiliu's true goal is not to seal Zhuyin, but to claim its power. To eliminate variables in the plan, Zhiliu imprisoned {nickname} at the Zhuyin Altar, turning against her.
Zhiliu employed every scheme at her disposal, resorting to deceit and exploiting {nickname}'s power without hesitation, all to slay the gods and bring down the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.

When Zhiliu was young, she was once trapped in a cave by a collapse. With no rescue in sight, one of those trapped grew desperate and tried to kill her for food. Keming, Kezhou's father, stopped him. During the struggle, the attacker fell against a sharp rock and died on the spot. When the Magistrates of Yingtian arrived, they judged Keming to have violated the Admonitions and executed him where he stood. His family was thereafter stigmatised as a criminal's kin and met with nothing but cold contempt.

This experience showed Zhiliu just how deeply the Nine Chapters of Dafeng had shaped the way people thought, and only hardened her resolve to overthrow it.

Zhiliu never intended to become a god. Her true aim was to free the people of Huaxu from their dependence on the gods, so that they might once again learn to face Deterioration, war, suffering, and crime by their own strength, and in doing so forge a new order for Huaxu.
A Luno of Huaxu who aspires to become its greatest Starweaver. She deeply admires Snow — the only horned Luno, and has voluntarily become her devoted follower.

A founding figure of Huaxu, architect of the Nine Chapters, and creator of Xuanheng Sect.
Active across Atlasia a millennium ago, she were a contemporary of Galea, the founding emperor of Hyperbria. Yang once wrote these words in the annals of Huaxu history: "Heaven and man, in perfect accord; yin and yang, in seamless harmony."

Yang possessed a rare ability known as the Art of Incense Discernment. By burning incense, she could influence and command nearby Filthoids, a power that would later give rise to Bi'an and the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. In essence, her gift was a weakened form of Resonance.
A Magistrate of Yingtian in Huaxu, who carries an aura of aloof detachment. He bears the weight of protecting all lives as his sacred duty, even at the cost of his own safety.

A former Drifter and fellow disciple of Kezhou, who now avoids him.
Kezhou states Yuming became the Magistrate of Yingtian due to an accident, not by choice.

During the massacre at Outer Peaks, Yuming's master, Yan Shanting, was killed. To save the people of Outer Peaks, Yuming was forced to kill Buxia, his junior fellow disciple under the same master, after Deterioration transformed her into a Filthoid. This led him to question the Drifters' defiance of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. In the end, he turned his back on the Drifters, accepted Taihao's invitation, and joined the Magistrates of Yingtian.

The leader of Haze Market, Huaxu's underground organization, who commands considerable respect among black market merchants.
His office is housed within a massive, wrecked merchant ship stranded on the western shore — its damaged hull concealing a surprisingly spacious interior.
A low-profile backer sponsor of Greenwich Archaeological Society.

The current heir of the Fu lineage, with reserved and detached demeanor.
She first met {nickname} while treating the wounded in Haze Market.

Fushu, active a century ago, contracted a fatal illness while treating patients during the Great Plague. Her sister Fufeng placed her in stasis to halt the disease's advance. A century later, Fufeng's successor developed a cure, reviving Fushu and allowing her to feel the world once more.

A swordsman who introduces himself as a Drifter, with unconstrained demeanor and chivalrous spirit. Kezhou became trapped in the Myriad-Snare Hunting Array while searching for his sword brother, where he met the similarly stranded {nickname}.

After parting ways with Kezhou at Crowsong Hollow, you met him again at the Hall of Adjudication. He had given himself up and petitioned the Magistrates of Yingtian for a Trial by Disputation. His true aim, however, was to assassinate Lord Argent in person, a plan as reckless as it was bold.

Kezhou was originally from Jiaolan Village. His father was Keming. Years ago, Keming was executed by the Magistrates of Yingtian for violating the Nine Chapters of Dafeng while trying to save a little girl. Kezhou and his mother were driven out of Jiaolan Village by the other villagers. Even so, Kezhou took after his father and never hesitated to stand up for what he believed was right.
A Wishen of unknown origin. Mischievous and unpredictable, it comes and goes without warning, living by a creed of absolute freedom.
Kezhou's "great-aunt". According to him, she has quite the temper, though he seems to have his own way of dealing with her.

Quartermaster of Outer Peaks and the seventeenth-generation heir to the Jishu Sect. As she is of the same generation as Kezhou's master's master, he addresses her as his "great-aunt". In fact, she is a vivacious young woman.
Su Yi is determined to win the Incense Proving not only to dispel prejudice against the Drifters, but also to clear her aunt Su Muzhe's name in the eyes of the public.

A founding figure of Huaxu, one of the architects of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, and founder of the Jishu Sect.

The Nine Chapters of Dafeng were not Yang's work alone. Ju was equally instrumental in bringing them into being. Seeking a way to stabilise and amplify Yang's power, he travelled far and wide in search of knowledge, even reaching the foot of the Tower in distant Elysium. Legend holds that he personally witnessed the Great Migration a thousand years ago.

In the end, Ju found the answer and brought it back to Huaxu, thereby making the Nine Chapters of Dafeng possible.

Yuming and Kezhou's shimei, a junior fellow disciple under the same master. As she neared adulthood, Deterioration took hold, and once transformed into a Filthoid, she killed many members of Outer Peaks, including Yan Shanting. In the end, Yuming was forced to kill her.
Zhiliu's master and the current leader of the Wuqiongzang Sect.

A well-known tale in Haojing, drawn from the exploits of several celebrated Drifters from roughly a decade ago.

Despite the name, the "Four Drifters" were in fact five people: Yan Shanting, the Master of the Thousand Peaks; Xing Xiangzi, the White Flame at Dawn; Su Muzhe, the River-Taming Swallow; and the Wen sisters, known together as the Wenzhu Wreath of Judgement.

Su Yi's aunt, and one of the Four Drifters, better known as the "River-Taming Swallow". In her early years, she worked for the Mechanistry Commission and was the first to introduce Su Yi to the Art of Mechwork.

When Su Yi was nine, Su Muzhe was exposed as having secretly communicated with the Drifters by means of mech-kites. She subsequently defected from Haojing and joined Outer Peaks.

During her time at the Mechanistry Commission, Su Muzhe designed the Miemeng Giant Bird to clear blocked waterways and prevent flooding. After she joined the Drifters, it was left to fall into disrepair.

When Su Yi was fourteen, someone with ulterior motives deliberately let Miemeng spiral out of control and used the crisis as bait, hoping to lure Su Muzhe back to Haojing so she could be executed in the name of the law. Though she knew it was a death trap, Su Muzhe returned all the same. For the sake of the people's safety, she ignored every attempt to stop her and stepped straight into it, determined to bring her creation back under control. Bi'an executed her on the spot. In her final moments, Su Muzhe tried to take control of Miemeng and fly it towards the Hall of Adjudication, hoping for one last glimpse of the god enthroned high within it, who ruled over the people below. Instead, Miemeng crashed, killing and injuring countless people. Her reason for returning to Haojing was later twisted into a claim that she had meant to use Miemeng to cause destruction.

The incident left a lasting mark on Su Yi. Six months later, she left home and joined Outer Peaks. Ever since, Su Yi has wished to clear her aunt's name and right the wrong done to her.
A mysterious {性别2:boy|girl} who appears in {nickname}'s recurring dream of the Sandrealm. {性别2:He|She} seems to possess knowledge of truths even {nickname} has yet to discover.
Under {性别2:his|her} guidance, {nickname} awakened the power known as "Resonance."

The true name of the mysterious {性别2:boy|girl} is {nickname2}.

{性别2:He|She} harbours a secret known to no one else — a voice that exists solely within {性别2:his|her} mind. This voice whispers of a strong desire for pain, blood, and death, relentlessly tempting {性别2:him|her} towards darkness.

A young soldier of the Hyperborean Empire, known for {性别2:his|her} exceptional combat prowess as a cadet at the Hyperborean Imperial Military College. The top graduate of the College's 133rd class, {性别2:he|she} earned the moniker "Pale Reaper."

Now serving as captain of the 13th Legion's Griffins squad, {性别2:he|she} has been deployed to the Lonza Fortress Operation.
Possesses only a few years' worth of memories and has no knowledge of {性别2:his|her} origins or early life.

Although {nickname2} still cannot remember anything from before four years ago, {性别2：his|her} actions in Mount Arcano successfully foiled Fulvis's schemes, provided the 13th Legion with key intel on the Catalyst, and made {性别2：his|her} a major contributor to the "Second Scion Program."

Before heading to Scarletriver, {nickname2} received a secret imperial decree personally delivered by Vergilius from Emperor Julius, ordering {性别2：him|her} to find an opportunity to assassinate Duke Servius of Scarletriver.
A mysterious figure who appeared one night at The Asphodel. They paid Camilla a large sum to rescue {nickname} from outside Icelake.

A Lunarian with exceptional smithing skills. Intrigued by {nickname}'s weapon Remanent Reminiscence, she chose to remain in Icelake for a time, aiding in the forging and refinement of arms for {nickname}.

A mysterious woman who appeared within the Thawing Caverns. She claims to be a Ferrywoman of the Misty Sea — one who can glimpse the thoughts of the departed and guide their lost souls back to the Misty Sea whence they came.

According to her, {nickname} bears an extraordinary fate and may one day cross the River of Life, to meet once more with the souls of the past in the heart of the Misty Sea.
The name of the vast continent upon which our story unfolds.

Stretching across the northern reaches of the Hyperborean Empire, the Vidofnir Mountains carve a jagged line through the continent of Atlasia. Beyond their frozen peaks lies the true Far North — home to the ancient fjords of Askard, where the oldest Charon tribes still dwell.

Scattered across the land of Atlasia, Heaventrees are crystalline growths named for their tree-like forms. Their size ranges from tiny saplings to towering giants. Within their translucent structures shimmer veins of blue light, and from their glimmering boughs, one may harvest the rare crystal known as Phoxene.

Believed to predate human history, the true origin of Heaventrees remains unknown. Ancient Elysian scholars regarded them as gifts from the heavens — a belief reflected in their name. That said, different cultures have referred to them by different names, and in some, early religious systems were built around their worship.

Their bounty, however, is not infinite. After prolonged extraction, the branches gradually wither and cease to yield Phoxene.

A rare mineral composed of interlocking pyramidal prisms. Its hues range from deep violet to midnight blue, and within its crystalline core shimmer lights that shift like starlight in motion — as though the night sky itself had taken solid form. Revered for its mesmerising beauty, Crystallo of Stella once sparked a frenzy among aristocrats and collectors, with demand driving prices to irrational heights.

In certain regions of the world, Crystallo of Stella has been used as an ingredient in medicinal remedies.

Within the Hyperborean Empire, a catastrophic incident in Flagson — a southern province — involving the crystal's medicinal use triggered widespread unrest. Since then, all civilian trade of the crystal has been strictly prohibited throughout the Empire.

When precisely refined into pharmaceutical compounds, Crystallo of Stella can produce various effects in Charon individuals showing early signs of Deterioration. Depending on the formulation, it may either accelerate or suppress the affliction's progression.
A vast natural lake located just outside Icelake. Due to the region's harsh climate, the lake remains frozen for most of the year — a characteristic that inspired the city's name.

A translucent crystal typically harvested from the "branches" of Heaventrees. It often exhibits a pale blue hue.

High-grade Phoxene is rich in combustible energy which, once refined, yields Phoxichor — a vital fuel source for modern machinery. The development of Phoxene-based technologies has significantly accelerated human civilisation. Throughout Atlasian history, the rise and fall of nations — as well as the outbreak of major wars — have been closely tied to the control and exploitation of Phoxene resources.

A highland northwest of Mistwharf, near the Zhuyin Altar.
Tainted by Zhuyin's leaking power, the area is now largely covered in a barren Gritblight. The ground is strewn with crystalline vegetation and jagged rock formations, giving the region its name. Mindless Filthoids and Sable Bi'an roam here, making the Gritblight Expanse a disaster zone impassable to ordinary people.

A geological hazard that emerged with the Scourge of Zhuyin, now spreading through Mistwharf. It manifests as violet crystalline dust that coats surfaces, saps life from flora and fauna, causing severe ecological damage.
The Mechanical Nexus, developed by Master Gongshang, can adsorb and remove Gritblight.
A Herb that grows in specific regions, known to neutralize the injuries caused by Bi'an.

Monstrous creatures once feared as the greatest threat to early civilisation. They roam across the Continent of Atlasia in a vast variety of forms, most of which are highly aggressive.

Though no longer a danger to civilisation itself — thanks to the rise of nation-states and the long march of war — they continue to pose a serious threat to individuals and small settlements to this day.

A highly intelligent non-human race whose appearance closely resembles that of human children. They are also called Lunos, most recognisable by their pale skin and white hair. Though long-lived, Lunarians show no visible signs of ageing. Deeply fond of humankind, they are often seen living peacefully alongside humans throughout the Atlasia continent.

Despite their largely uniform appearance, most Lunarians demonstrate a natural aptitude in a specific field — smithing, commerce, investment, and the like.

Snow, however — the one always flitting about The Asphodel — appears to be an exception... unless talking herself up qualifies as a legitimate skill.

The Charon — a race marked by their horns and distinctive spines — possesses greater physical resilience than ordinary humans, known collectively as the Solarian. They are also highly adaptable to both heat and cold.

The name "Charon" originates from an ancient creation myth passed down among their kind — of a divine vessel said to ferry newborn souls into the world of the living.

Within the Hyperborean Empire, the Charon make up about 20% of the population, and are believed to carry a cursed lineage and are often branded as "Demon's Children." As a result, they are stripped of the basic rights granted to the Solarian and face systemic discrimination throughout the Empire.

As they approach adulthood, the Charon undergo a singular transformation known as the Awakening.

For most, the change is subtle — if it manifests at all. But among a gifted few, the Awakening gives rise to arcane abilities, referred to across the Empire as "magic." These powers vary greatly between individuals in both form and strength. Those who manifest such abilities are known as Daimons.

In rare cases, the Awakening collapses into a condition known as Deterioration. Those afflicted gradually lose their humanity — memories, reason, even identity — and ultimately transform into an especially destructive variant of Filthoid, far more dangerous than those typically found in the wild. No known cure exists.

It is this dread of Deterioration that drives the Solarian to view the Charon as an existential threat.

According to Hyperborean historical records, the Charon once launched a continent-wide war during the Sacred Tower Era over two millennia ago, indiscriminately slaughtering Solarians and driving them to the brink of extinction. This history is frequently cited as a key reason why Charon citizens continue to face deep-rooted stigma and remain denied equal civil rights within the Empire.

A massive creature that lurks within the ruins of Glevum Pit, named for its obsession with hoarding crystalline fragments. Though beastlike in appearance, parts of its body resemble human anatomy — suggesting it may not have always been a monster.

The creature known as the Crystalophile was once a young miner named Hamel Dickinson, who went missing forty years ago.

As a young man, Dickinson ventured alone into the mines in search of a legendary gemstone, intending to elope with the girl he loved — Hilin. However, deep within the tunnels, he lost his sanity and eventually transformed into a monster.

Driven, perhaps, by the lingering force of obsession, the creature continued to amass glittering stones long after his transformation, as if still longing to present them to his beloved.

Daimons are gifted Charon individuals who awaken to unique powers. These abilities — varying in form and intensity — are often linked to one's bloodline. Within the Hyperborean Empire, such powers are regarded as evil and are commonly branded as "magic."

A rare condition unique to the Charon, for which no cure exists within the Hyperborean Empire.

Early signs of Deterioration typically appear before adulthood. Affected individuals develop markings resembling severe burn scars, often accompanied by sensory decline, bouts of aggression, and mental instability. Upon reaching the point of "Awakening," the afflicted experience a complete loss of memory and emotion, ultimately transforming into an exceptionally powerful variant of Filthoid — entities marked by immense strength and indiscriminate violence.

To prevent the spread of such threats, any Charon citizen exhibiting signs of Deterioration is subject to immediate execution by the Escort. Those who harbour or assist a Deteriorator are deemed complicit in the threat and are subject to the same punishment.

The most widespread group of ordinary humans across the continent of Atlasia.

The term Solarian was originally coined to distinguish regular humans from the Charon in social discourse. Over time, it became the widely accepted label for this demographic. The word Sola derives from an ancient Atlasian language, meaning "sun."

Even today, some radical Solarian supremacists reject the term altogether, arguing that "true humans" should not require a label that places them on equal footing with other races.
Known among the people as "Lord Argent", Taihao is the revered god of Huaxu — the living embodiment of the heavenly way, the will of the Nine Chapters.

Guardian and enforcer of Huaxu, acting by the will of the Nine Chapters. It's a divine beast with a wolf's head, bestial body, white fur and golden horns.
When the Nine Chapters are broken, Bi'an arrives to deliver judgment, ensuring the realm's enduring peace.

Bi'an is transformed from a nearly adult Loongscion.
Some scholars theorize that Bi'an share the same nature as Filthoids. Their creation is believed to be the result of the deterioration process being influenced by the Nine Chapters. The precise mechanism, however, remains unknown.

Similar in form to a Bi'an, but jet-black in color. Recently appeared near Mistwharf, these are chaotic aberrations born of the Scourge of Zhuyin, beyond the control of the Nine Chapters.
They indiscriminately attack travelers in the wilds, severely disrupting public safety. Notably, assaulting a Sable Bi'an does not incur punishment from the Nine Chapters.

A malevolent deity from Huaxu's ancient legends, rival to Taihao, now sealed beyond Mistwharf. Its deranged power has leaked out, creating the Scourge of Zhuyin.
A century ago, Zhuyin first awoke and was subdued only through a massive concerted effort. It has now awakened for a second time.
One of the two revered deities, alongside Taihao, who jointly safeguarded Huaxu at the founding of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. Taihao governed law, while Zhuyin presided over the mind.
Following the Battle of Shuli centuries ago, Zhuyin was sealed and expelled from the Nine Chapters, and its legacy as a revered deity was gradually forgotten by the world.

Wishens are special beings formed from the dying regrets of individuals in Huaxu, influenced by the pervasive incense in the air.
They typically lose most of their memories and exhibit degraded speech and cognitive abilities.
Invisible to ordinary people, they can only be perceived by children and those with unique energy. Though unable to directly interact with the physical world, they can subtly influence small objects. Folklore about Wishen, in various forms, persists throughout Huaxu.
Wishens are sustained by their lingering regrets, and will dissipate once these regrets are resolved.

A recurring dream {nickname} has experienced since childhood. In it, white sand falls endlessly from the heavens, veiling the sky in a pale shroud. A solitary figure appears where the sand and sky meet, though its outline remains obscured.

A hidden power that awakened within {nickname} during {性别:his|her} battle against Sibylle Mason, guided by the voice of the figure in {性别:his|her} dream.

At the moment of its first emergence, {nickname} and Berenica became one — their strength significantly enhanced through the force of {nickname}'s will.

At its core, Resonance is a force of attunement. Those who master it may channel their own energy to amplify the magic of nearby Daimons or Filthoids through sheer force of will. In rare and exceptional cases, the wielder of this power may temporarily merge with another individual, gaining full control over their movements and abilities.

Decades ago, an individual capable of wielding Resonance incited widespread unrest within the Empire. They were ultimately executed by Arboreal Crucifixion — the highest form of capital punishment in Hyperborea.
According to Zhiliu, the true nature of Resonance lies in its power to guide and command. It was through this power that Huaxu's ancestor Yang founded the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.

The supreme law governing all of Huaxu.
All within its borders must obey its precepts, lest they face punishment enforced by Bi'an or Magistrate of Yingtian. Beyond forbidding acts like killing and robbery, it can suppress Filthoids within its domain, stripping them of their ferocity.
The people's revered deity, Taihao, is the living embodiment of its will.

Although designed to eliminate crime, the Nine Chapters' rigid enforcement criteria create loopholes that some exploit.
For instance, a black market merchant swindled a young girl's father by tampering with a contract — an act the Nine Chapters failed to prevent due to its inflexible judgment.

At its core, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng are a vast system founded upon magic. At the root of that system lies Yang's Art of Incense Discernment, which enabled her to command nearby Filthoids.

To preserve that art in permanent form, Ju travelled far beyond Huaxu and eventually discovered an ancient sacrificial rite that could serve as its foundation. With his gift for engineering, he constructed the Taixu Mausoleum. When it was completed, Yang, Ju, and many forebears of the Loongscions gave their lives, thereby establishing the sacrifice that sustains the Nine Chapters of Dafeng to this day. Once the rite was established, Taihao and Zhuyin took shape through the incense that suffused the land. As heirs to their forebears' will, they have governed Huaxu ever since.

After the Battle of Shuli, Zhuyin was sealed away, and the balance between heart and principle was broken. Taihao became the embodiment of absolute order, while Zhuyin, bereft of reason and consumed by unending wrath, wrought destruction time and again. From that point on, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng began to grow rigid.

Now that the balance between heart and principle has been restored and Zhuyin has returned to their rightful place, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng stand on the verge of reform. The ancient Trial by Disputation will also be revived, so that mortals and gods may govern Huaxu together.

A calamity that befell Huaxu, radiating from the Gritblight Expanse and primarily affecting Mistwharf. Its spread has severed trade routes, causing severe disruption to daily life.
The Scourge manifests chiefly in two forms: the Sable Bi'an and Gritblight.
A healing art passed down through the Fu lineage. Its power flows directly from the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.
The Art of Ephemerality works by using Zhuyous' own vitality as a conduit to purge impurities from the patient. Frequent use places a heavy physical burden on the practitioner.

A hypothetical entity in natural philosophy. Huaxu scholars believe the air is permeated by a colorless, odorless substance that provides energy for all things. When activated by incense, this substance becomes the medium through which the Nine Chapters operate. Gritblight is considered the tangible form of condensed Taixu — a physical manifestation of its existence.
Mysterious runes drifting throughout Huaxu, formed from the condensation of excess Taixu in the air.
An anomalous dimension born when the Spring of Yu was tainted by the Scourge of Zhuyin. Within it, souls gradually forget all worldly attachments, becoming eternally lost.
One of the most ancient rites, handed down since time immemorial. Those who enter into a Covenant of Souls share both life and power.

entries.title: Temple of the Goddess of Fate

texts.text:
The crumbling ruins of an ancient Elysian temple, built atop the hills of Purgatorio Island. Dedicated to the Goddess of the Full Moon and Fate, it once served as a revered site of pilgrimage.

A millennium ago, during the Great Migration, it was ravaged by waves of Iconoclasm and has remained unrestored ever since.

One of the most pivotal events in early Hyperborean history.
According to official imperial records, near the end of the Great Migration a millennium ago, a band of migrants led by Dis Galea — later crowned as Dis Ⅰ — pressed northward into the southern tundras of the Vidofnir Mountains, now part of the Cocytus Region. There, they clashed intermittently with the local Charon tribes. Seeking peace, the magnanimous Dis Galea brokered an accord with the Charon tribes: a celebration would be held beside Lamenting Lake to mark the dawn of peace. But the gathering became a blood-soaked snare. Feigning goodwill, the Charon launched a massacre that very night. Nearly all the Solarian were slain. Only Dis escaped — shielded by the final sacrifice of his brother, Soranus Galea.
In the wake of the "Night of Lamenting Lake," Dis buried Soranus with a heavy heart and withdrew to the southern Hyperborean plains. Over the next decade, he rebuilt his forces. With overwhelming numbers and honed tactics, he repelled the raiding Charon and led countless triumphs against the mighty Deteriorators. Through fire, blood, and tears, he unified the plains — and then turned north once more. Dis marched again upon Lamenting Lake, crushed the tribes that had betrayed him, and raised the fortress of Icelake Keep upon its shores — the precursor to what would later become the city of Icelake. There, in the year 20 of the New Calendar, he was crowned Dis Ⅰ, and the Hyperborean Empire was born.
Yet as he stood before his sworn enemies, Dis Ⅰ chose neither vengeance nor retribution. He chose peace — and forgiveness. Through the Edict of Icelake Keep, he proclaimed the Charon to be children of Hyperborea all the same, and bound them beneath the Empire's banner.
To honour the peacemaker who founded their homeland, the citizens of Icelake gather each year on the day of the Edict's decree to celebrate the Silvercandle Carnival — a festival of peace and unity.

A civil war fought centuries ago between the Xuanheng Sect and Jishu Sect on Crowsong Hollow, near Mistwharf.
The conflict profoundly reshaped Huaxu. After Shuli, enforcement of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng became significantly stricter, the Jishu Sect declined, and the Art of Mechwork was heavily restricted. The battle remains a cultural byword for the calamity of war in Huaxu.

The Battle of Shuli was in fact sparked by an accident. Tensions between the Jishu Sect and the Xuanheng Sect had already been simmering for some time. The latter sent forces to Crowsong Hollow to investigate rumours that the Jishu Sect intended to secede. On that fog-shrouded day, as the two sides faced off in uneasy silence, a war automaton suddenly spun out of control, and the conflict erupted.

The war's true origin has long since been buried by time, and few now care to question it. Only the stone stele deep within the Labyrinth of Yanyin still bears silent witness to the truth.

The Great Plague was a devastating epidemic that struck Mistwharf a century ago, triggered by the first Scourge of Zhuyin. It inflicted countless casualties, only receding after Zhuyin itself was sealed away.

After the battle with Zhuyin, Zhiliu took {nickname} away and revealed the future through three prophecies.
The First Symbol — Overreach: the foe soaring beyond bounds invites a crushing descent.
{nickname} would ascend to the utmost heights, confront Lord Argent, and live to tell the tale.

Zhiliu's "prophecies" are less prophecies than a suggestion implanted deep within {nickname}'s mind — in other words, a form of hypnosis. She must be stopped before those "prophecies" are allowed to come to pass.

The Second Symbol — Thaw: Essence to embrace, facade to renounce; disbandment for the whole. A marsh dries for the mountain's sake — one loss to preserve the whole.
{nickname} would take shelter deep in the mountains, compromising the Outer Peaks, drawing the Sentinels of Juntian to their gates.
Zhiliu's aim is to lure the Sentinels away while Taihao lies wounded, so that she can carry out her plan to kill a god.

The Third Symbol — Upheaval: the mighty changes with the tiger's resolve; yet darkness falls from heavens. A mausoleum hangs in the void; the constellations yield to a new sovereign.
Within the Taixu Mausoleum, Zhiliu intends to strengthen Zhuyin at the cost of her own life, setting the two Loong gods against one another. She asks {nickname} to kill her at the critical moment and bring it all to an end. Zhiliu's death would trigger a backlash from the Covenant of Souls that would reach both Taihao and Zhuyin, bringing even the gods to their end. If all goes as she intends, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng may at last be overthrown.

An uprising launched by the Forsakens in the southern reaches of the Empire. During the conflict, a Heaventree was set ablaze, preventing Imperial airships from approaching the area.

The rebellion was eventually suppressed under the command of Sibylle Mason.

In Charon mythology, the Misty Sea is believed to be the birthplace of all life. It is said that the Sacred Tree took root amidst its haze, blooming with pure white blossoms, from which Mother Embla emerged and created the living world.

The Charon hold that all departed souls eventually return to the Misty Sea — and that new life, too, rises from its depths.

The primordial deities in the ancient faith of the Charons.
In their myths, the Mother Embla was born from a pure white blossom of the sacred Heaventree, she created all things — and from her came Father Ask. Together, they gave birth to the first of the Charons.
Later, bearer of the power of death, became a vessel of calamity. In the end, it was he who brought ruin to the world — the cataclysm called Ragnarok. To protect her children, Embla, keeper of the power of life, sacrificed herself. Her soul scattered into the sea， and at last, returned to the Misty Sea. Ask's body became the land and his arms, upraised, became the mountains, still reaching for the gods... who no longer come.
Another tale continues this creation myth. In it, Embla and Ask did not fade away, but were born anew in a world reshaped by the cataclysm. They would bring about another end, and another rebirth, trapping the world and all life in an endless cycle of dawn and twilight.

A finely crafted, razor-sharp white sword owned by {nickname}. Once believed to be an ordinary weapon, it is in fact the key to a hidden passage within the temple. According to Berenica, the sword was left behind by someone who once knew them well.

In a desperate attempt to save his daughter Hayley from the onset of Deterioration, Henrik devoted himself to developing a suppression serum. Despite his efforts, the research failed to halt her transformation, and the project was abandoned following her death.

Years later, Henrik resumed his study, this time with the aim of aiding other afflicted children. Using the rare material Crystallo of Stella, he succeeded in creating a prototype of the Deterioration Suppression Serum. However, the formula remained untested, and its effects were uncertain.

Psyche, a patient under his care, volunteered to become the first test subject. The serum unexpectedly accelerated the progression of Deterioration and triggered an early onset, causing her to enter a violent state in which she injured Henrik.

A clandestine initiative conducted by The Spathatoi, a division of the Royal Alchemy Academy of Hyperborea, overseen directly by Chief Sibylle of the 13th Legion. The experiment centres on "No. 0." To advance the programme, Fulvis was dispatched to Flagson to locate a crucial "catalyst" — though no viable lead has surfaced thus far.
Through Catalyst, one can continuously create replicas based on a single prototype. The Catalyst is most likely in the hands of Mother Bunny, the master of Paradise Village.
The Catalyst required for the Second Scion Program is Ada's innate power of replication.

Under the pretext of military recruitment, the 6th Legion of Hyperborea has long enlisted physically robust Charon recruits into closed training programmes, claiming that outstanding performance could earn them the prestigious title of Laurelled Charon. In truth, the 6th Legion has been operating in collusion with the Spathatoi in Icelake, secretly selecting candidates with latent potential and subjecting them to covert augmentation trials — part of a larger initiative to develop bio-engineered weapons for warfare.

During the investigation into the Charon Hunt, Major Lynn uncovered evidence of the 6th Legion's secret experiments. She reported her findings to Sibylle Mason, chief of the 13th Legion, but was ordered to cease any further inquiry.

A substance widely used throughout Huaxu, prepared from specific ingredients and through a meticulous process. Incense burners are kept lit across the land, ensuring its fragrance perpetually lingers in the air. People also commonly carry personal incense sachets. It is a defining regional feature of Huaxu.
When blessed, incense can protect the wearer or briefly ward off foes. Once its power is spent, the wearer must visit an Argent Loong Temple for renewed blessing — a process called "Replenishment".

Incense is the vital medium that sustains the Nine Chapters. The law's influence extends only where its fragrance permeates.
Within Huaxu, two methods ensure its continuity: daily offerings made voluntarily by the people, and large-scale, state-organized ceremonies. The ubiquitous burners and censers are maintained by Xuanheng Sect, ensuring the fragrant smoke never fades.

A Jishu Sect-crafted device. This cube, with its embedded energy core, was custom-made for Zhiliu by the black market to harvest Zhuyin Scales. It combines powerful adsorption with multiple functions.
A primordial mechanical trap, long dormant within Crowsong Hollow, was accidentally triggered during Mr. Qiu's hunting operation.

A device developed by the Drifters to conceal their base from the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. It removes all traces of incense from the air while emitting a decoy signal. With nothing for the Nine Chapters to lock onto, their tracking is rendered ineffective, while the false signal prevents Lord Argent from detecting the anomaly.

The Juzi Patrol Nexus, Type Ⅱ: Qingluan is a mechapuppet prepared by Su Yi specifically for the Incense Proving, modelled after the Yi-bird. As its full name is rather unwieldy, it is usually shortened to Qingluan Type Ⅱ.

After a complaint was lodged against the Qingluan Type Ⅱ during the competition, it was placed in storage for inspection. Later that night, it was sabotaged. Fortunately, Su Yi had intended to dismantle it and rebuild it as a more powerful model anyway.

Desperate to win, Su Yi pushed the Qingluan Type Ⅱ beyond its limits during the match, causing it to explode. The blast occurred in a sparsely populated area and resulted in no casualties or property damage.

A rail vehicle made up of multiple carriages pulled by a Phoxichor-powered engine along fixed tracks. Though a relatively recent invention, trains have already become the preferred means of travel for Imperial citizens thanks to their speed and comfort — even if much of their capacity is still reserved for troop movements and military supplies.

Unfortunately, fares remain prohibitively expensive, putting rail travel out of reach for most ordinary households.
Sibylle Mason's private express train, named after her codename. On rare occasions, it is deployed for special operations.

A device commonly used by the Forsakens for sabotage. In its simplest form, a bomb consists of three parts: a casing, an explosive charge, and a fuse.

Though it does not always cause heavy casualties, it is highly effective at spreading panic and disrupting public order.

The latest achievement of Hyperborean alchemical engineering. Powered by high-performance Phoxichor engines, these steel vessels are capable of taking to the skies and are exceedingly difficult to shoot down. Their arrival has opened an entirely new dimension in warfare. Since their invention, the outcome of a battle has no longer been determined by what happens on the ground, but by how quickly airships can reach the battlefield. As a result, the Empire's rule has grown ever more secure.

A Phoxichor-powered cannon mounted at the front of the train, capable of destroying any target within its line of sight. Trains were originally developed for military use, serving not only to transport troops and supplies but also as mobile weapons platforms. Like iron behemoths, they move along the Empire's rails, carrying both cargo and firepower.

A long-established opera troupe with an extensive touring history across Hyperborea. Its current director is Ms Putsch, and its members include the celebrated soprano Violetta. In recent years, the troupe has taken up long-term residence at the Galea Theatre in Icelake — rumour has it this arrangement was made at Violetta's personal request.

A celebrated operatic work inspired by a folk tale from Icelake. It tells the story of a frost fairy who dwells in a snowy fortress and becomes friends with a human girl and her younger brother. Renowned for its lyrical beauty and deep resonance with Icelake's wintry landscape, the opera has long remained a beloved classic — once the most frequently performed piece at the Galea Theatre.
The production was suspended for two years following a violent on-stage altercation at the Galea Theatre.

Beneath its fairytale charm lies a tragic ending: to protect the human children, the frost fairy forsakes their castle and willingly transforms into a beast. With their promise fulfilled, the fairy falls into eternal slumber beneath the frozen earth.
A property owned by Henrik, long listed for sale but never sold due to his cold and uncooperative manner. It now serves as a temporary place of shelter for {nickname} in Icelake.
According to Henrik's will, ownership of the house was transferred to Ms Lina, who subsequently waived {nickname}'s rent and welcomed {性别:him|her} to stay indefinitely.

A grand, stately inn located in northern Icelake. Its gates have long remained closed to the public.

Though known as an inn, it seldom — if ever — welcomes travellers.

Locals whisper of strange odours drifting from its upper windows and ghostly sobs echoing through the night. Many have come to call it a haunted house.
All its lodgers are youths under the age of twenty, each personally selected by Henrik. Once brought in, none ever leave.

Henrik's study is a forbidden area within the inn — no one but he is permitted to enter. He spends most of his time behind its locked door, conducting private research. The young residents, all afflicted with a certain illness, are often observed displaying unnatural behaviours.

In truth, the inn serves as a hospice for children showing early signs of Deterioration. After losing his daughter Hayley to the condition, Henrik devoted himself to what he calls the Slumber Project — a silent mission to shelter these doomed children from military execution orders. Disguised as a guesthouse, Hypnos' House offers them a peaceful end — a place where they may leave this ruthless world as they entered it: as human, not as a grotesque beast.

The busiest tavern in Icelake, The Asphodel welcomes all manner of patrons — from inner-city nobles to drifters from the slums. Among them are more than a few dangerous types, and clashes — verbal or otherwise — are an almost daily occurrence. Yet thanks to the masterful tact and diplomacy of its proprietress, Camilla, few such incidents ever escalate into true conflict. In a way, The Asphodel may be the most disorderly yet most peaceful place in the entire city.

Beyond serving food and drink, the tavern also functions as a hub for Phoxhunters. Both clients and Phoxhunters can post or accept tasks here, with Camilla acting as an impartial broker to ensure payment, confidentiality, and safety for both sides.

Some claim the tavern is involved in more illicit dealings behind the scenes. But lacking solid proof, such talk remains mere tavern gossip — hardly something the Escort would concern itself with.

Phoxhunters are a distinct profession that originated in Icelake, loosely comparable to bounty hunters. They first emerged by taking on jobs to collect Phoxene, a practice that gave rise to their name. Even after the Phoxene trade was monopolised by the Empire and privileged merchant classes, the profession persisted — gradually evolving beyond its original purpose. Today, Phoxhunters take on nearly any task, from trivial errands to deadly missions. So long as the price is right, there is always someone willing to take the risk.

In Icelake, Phoxhunters typically gather at a local tavern called The Asphodel, where Camilla, the proprietress, acts as a broker between clients and Phoxhunters. The work is often dangerous, but the generous pay and open access — regardless of background — make it especially attractive to many Charons.

Because Phoxhunters rarely discriminate between clients, many lower-class Charons — unable to seek protection through official channels — turn to them in times of need. Over time, this informal force has come to fill the void left by the city's law enforcement, offering a semblance of order where official authority cannot reach.
A series of murders that took place in Icelake. The assailant struck in the early hours of 22 and 25 November, claiming the lives of nineteen Charon victims. {nickname} was the only known survivor.
According to eyewitness accounts, the perpetrator was a monstrous entity hiding within the city's sewer system.
Officer Rhythm Fischer and the Noctoyagers engaged the entity underground. Although they managed to inflict significant damage, they were forced to retreat following an ambush by a second assailant.

After initially escaping, the perpetrator shifted to a new pattern of attacks. Infiltrating the inner city, it killed several Solarian citizens and left behind graffiti bearing anti-Solarian slogans. This escalation drew the attention of Hyperborea's upper echelons, prompting direct intervention by the 13th Legion.

The two assailants were later revealed to be subjects of a covert experiment conducted by the 6th Legion — Charon individuals who had undergone forced alchemical augmentation. In an effort to expose the truth behind these experiments, one of them — still retaining fragments of reason — aligned with the Forsakens and carried out targeted attacks in the inner city, aiming to provoke a formal investigation by the 13th Legion. However, upon realising that the Legion intended to suppress the truth, the assailant turned on their Forsaken allies, killing their own handlers.

The case concluded with the death of one assailant and the capture of the other by the 13th Legion. Due to its connection with classified military operations, the full details of the incident were never disclosed to the public.

A longstanding Icelake tradition dating back to the founding days of Hyperborea. On the night of the festival, citizens don masks and costumes, gathering at the candlelit Galea Theatre to enjoy performances and dance until dawn.

In an otherwise rigid and hierarchical city, this is the one night when identities and origins are momentarily cast aside — a fleeting sense of freedom that may explain why the festival has endured, despite being so at odds with Icelake's usual atmosphere.

A Huaxu term for merchants engaged in foreign trade. The name reflects their original vision: to connect isolated places across the continent like stars forming a constellation.
Masters of navigation and trade, Starweavers possess the unique skill of celestial wayfinding, enabling them to overcome the most perilous sailing conditions. Their reach extends to even the most remote corners of Atlasia.

Huaxu's name for Charons.
Unlike in Hyperborean Empire, Huaxu's people view Charons as an auspicious race that safeguards the nation. As such, the Loongscion is a revered presence in Huaxu.
Large stone tablets inscribed with the laws of the Nine Chapters. Erected in prominent locations across Huaxu, they serve as a perpetual reminder to all.
{nickname} can directly perceive the steles' contents. This is seemingly linked to the power of Resonance.

Enforcers within the Nine Chapters system, a higher rank than Bi'an. They too are transformed from Loongscions. By reasoning similar to Bi'an, scholars theorize the Magistrate of Yingtianare what would commonly be termed "Daimon."
Their power flows from the Nine Chapters. So long as their spine escapes fatal harm, they can gradually recover from wounds by drawing energy from this supreme law.

Dedicated to Taihao, these temples are found throughout Huaxu. The largest in Mistwharf stands just outside EverSpring.
Here, people have their incense sachets blessed and convey their spiritual devotion to heaven.

A unique Huaxu profession, akin to physicians.
Empowered by the Nine Chapters of Dafeng with healing magic, they hold a revered role in society.
Their abilities are hereditary. With the rise of pharmacology over the past century, their arts have waned, leaving few practitioners today.
The ancestral medical clinic of the Fu family, nestled among the apricot groves north of Mistwharf. A place where people seek healing.

A traditional Huaxu festival held once every four years, its origins dating back to the earliest days of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. During the Rite, the people of Huaxu gather at the Hall of Adjudication under the guidance of the Rite Envoy to offer incense to Lord Argent, praying for lasting peace and prosperity throughout the realm. It is regarded as one of the central ceremonies that keep the Nine Chapters of Dafeng functioning.
