A major competition held during the Grand Incense Rite. Its purpose is to select the Rite Envoy, who will ascend to the summit of the Hall of Adjudication and preside over the ceremonial rites. As the Rite Envoy is granted an audience with Lord Argent, their words carry considerable weight and may influence public sentiment for a time. For this reason, many seek to win the Incense Proving and claim the title. The form of the competition has varied from one Rite to the next.

Following the reform of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, this year's Incense Proving will be held in a new format known as "Rivalry".

Teams enter a designated arena and fight for Civil and Martial Tokens by eliminating Filthoids or collecting treasures. Final rankings are determined by each team's total token count.

Elite enforcers charged with guarding the Hall of Adjudication and the heart of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. The Sentinels of Juntian wield power far beyond that of ordinary Magistrates of Yingtian, sustained by the Nine Chapters themselves.

The lowest-class carriage at the very rear of the train. With little inside beyond its bare metal frame, it is reserved for those who simply need to get from one place to another, with no expectation of comfort or pleasure in the journey. As for security... there is scarcely any to speak of.

The most ordinary carriage on the train. "Standard" though it may be, a ticket still costs more than most people can afford without years of saving. Compared with the Rat Tin, however, its interior already feels positively luxurious.

The carriage occupied by the train's guards, who are responsible for maintaining order on board. Positioned ahead of the standard carriage, it also serves, to some extent, as a buffer between ordinary passengers and those in first class. In that respect, their role is much the same as that of guards and soldiers anywhere else: to keep order, and to keep people in their place.

The service carriage used by the attendants serving the train's first-class passengers. Located between the guard carriage and the first-class carriage, it is where meals are prepared and dishes for private banquets are made ready whenever the first-class passengers call for them.

The foremost passenger carriage, fitted with luxuries befitting its exorbitant fare. People sometimes joke that this is the true heart of the train, and that all the other carriages are little more than freight wagons. Here, passengers of rank enjoy the journey in comfort while exchanging news and information. In every respect save one — it reaches its destination no sooner than any other carriage — it stands apart from the rest of the train as a world of its own.

An organisation made up of nobles, merchants, and certain members of the station guard who support Stationmaster Eisenbahn. Its main activities centre on expressing admiration for Eisenbahn and producing memorabilia in his likeness, some of which sells for surprisingly high prices.

Eisenbahn himself, however, seems to keep the group at arm's length... for reasons that remain unclear.
A special festival of Arcano.
According to the villagers, the Parade is a celebration where all villagers work together to make the village a better place.

During the Parade, a game is held. The participant with the highest number of votes in the game is eliminated.
The Parade is essentially a loyalty test conducted by Mother Bunny on the residents of the paradise. Players who violate the rules of paradise are executed.

Every resident of Arcano has a unique arcana name, each carrying a different meaning and essence: "The Fool", "The Magician", "The High Priestess", "The Empress", "The Emperor", "The Hierophant", "The Lovers", "The Chariot", "Strength", "The Hermit", "Wheel of Fortune", "Justice", "The Hanged Man", "Death", "Temperance", "The Devil", "The Tower", "The Star", "The Moon", "The Sun", "Judgement", "The World". These nameplates signify that all who bear them are part of the paradise family.

Once the largest Phoxene mine in northern Hyperborea. The veins have long since run dry, and though several nearby factories remain in operation, the mine itself has been abandoned. Its hollowed depths are now a den for Filthoids.

Located at the junction between Icelake's inner and outer districts, Galea Theatre has stood for centuries, bearing witness to the city's rise and decline.

It remains the only venue in the outer city where nobles and aristocrats are still frequently seen.

Originally a self-organised cooperative formed by a handful of fishermen, the Icelake Fisheries grew in scale following the decline of local mining and the rise of the fishing industry. It was later restructured under government oversight and now serves as the city's official fisheries management body.

A major guild based in Mistwharf plains. It functions as Starweavers' trade association and serves as the largest commercial hub in Haojing. EverSpring operates under the Ministry of Fortune, which oversees Huaxu's finance and trade.

A prestigious non-governmental scholarly organization operating across borders, dedicated to the vision of returning lost relics to the world. It conducts archaeological projects throughout Atlasia, focusing on exploring ancient ruins, preserving artifacts, and uncovering historical truths.
The Society accepts funding from diverse sources and was once a fashionable cause among high society — its honorary members have even included a former Hyperbrian Empress.

A renowned apothecary in Haojing. Legend has it that its founder came from House Fu, a branch of the Zhuyou clan famed for the healing art known as the Art of Ephemerality. She chose to leave that tradition behind, however, and devote herself instead to herbal medicine, giving rise to what would become Zesheng Pharmacy. After decades of growth, it now has a large number of disciples and apprentices.

A factory complex located beneath Bloomfield Station, employing a large workforce. It is used for train maintenance, as well as the storage and processing of Phoxichor. In sharp contrast to the bustle of the station above, the ironworks feels subdued.

Unlike traditional stone buildings, Bloomfield Station is built with a steel frame and a glass roof, giving it abundant natural light and making it one of Icelake's most recognisable landmarks.

The steelwork cleaners are responsible for clearing dust and bird nests from the station's metal framework. The role is usually taken on by nimble, sharp-witted children.

A clandestine association of labourers working at Bloomfield Station, open only to those who have proven they can endure hard work.

Its members offer one another limited support, yet the identity of the union's leader — and its true purpose — remain shrouded in mystery.

The official military education institution of the Hyperborean Empire. It is responsible for the recruitment and training of personnel for the Hyperborean Legion, including both combat troops and logistics units.

The highest form of capital punishment in Hyperborean Empire, reserved for severe political crimes such as treason or espionage. The condemned is bound in thorned vines and suspended upside down from the Heaventree at the centre of Dismania, left to die from blood loss.

An honorary title awarded by the Hyperborean Empire to Charon individuals who have rendered exceptional service. Those granted this distinction are accorded the same civil rights as Solarian citizens.
The Empire's highest legal statute. According to historical records, its earliest draft was personally written by Dis I, the founding emperor.

A unique official title in Huaxu, granted by the mandate of heaven.
A Loongscion favoured by this mandate may be elevated to this position, receiving special authority and status to oversee the nation's administration.

A guardian sect of Huaxu, founded by Yang, architect of the Nine Chapters.
The Sect first discovered incense's extraordinary properties in antiquity and has preserved its use as a proprietary art. Today, it manages state incense ceremonies and maintains order in Argent Loong Temples. One of Huaxu's three main administrative bodies, the Ministry of Rites, operates under its direct control.
A temporary decree issued by EverSpring after the Scourge of Zhuyin began to spread. It prohibits commercial travel through certain areas, with the sole aim of ensuring Starweaver safety.

Once a guardian sect of Huaxu, now in decline. The Jishu Sect excels in crafting both mechapuppets and tools powered by Phoxene, which see widespread use across Huaxu's civil sectors. One of Huaxu's three main administrative bodies, the Ministry of Works, was formerly under its direction.

The most magnificent structure in Haojing. Spanning the peaks of twin mountains and rising above the clouds, it towers over the entire capital. Legend holds that it is also the divine residence where Lord Argent descends to dwell. The Hall stands as both the symbol of Haojing and the political centre of Huaxu.
One of the Three Ministries of Huaxu. It oversees the country's economy, trade networks, and tax administration.

An institution under the Ministry of Rites, staffed primarily by members of the Xuanheng Sect. It serves as Haojing's official authority on incense supply, incense preparation, and the rites and protocols governing incense offerings.

An institution under the Ministry of Works, composed largely of members of the Jishu Sect. It is responsible for the construction of Haojing's infrastructure and the maintenance of its public facilities.

In ancient Huaxu, when a case proved too difficult to resolve, the great bell atop the Hall of Adjudication would toll. Lord Argent and mortals would then gather at the Hall's summit to deliberate the matter together in a process known as Trial by Disputation. The practice has long since been abolished, and today few even know it ever existed.

Huaxu once passed through an age when more than a hundred sects contended for supremacy. Many unorthodox sects from that era survive to this day, keeping their distance from the outside world. The Wuqiongzang Sect is among them, known for its mastery of divination and esoteric calculation. Its practitioners are said to glimpse possible futures through hexagrams and, through certain specialised techniques, even influence the human mind.

An ancient artefact jointly forged by Yang and Ju when the Nine Chapters of Dafeng were founded, meant to preserve the balance between heart and principle. The Jade of Equilibrium was divided into two halves, one held by the Xuanheng Sect and the other by the Jishu Sect. The Jishu Sect's half, however, vanished after the Battle of Shuli.

During the clash with Taihao, and later in the depths of the Labyrinth of Yanyin, {nickname} recovered the two halves one after the other, making the Jade of Equilibrium whole once more.

A title held by one of the seven highest-ranking members of the Hazering, the conclave regarded as the supreme authority of the Forsakens.

The Beast-King is chiefly responsible for combat operations, territorial expansion, and the planning of actions against the Empire.

A secluded island adrift in international waters, lying between Hyperborea and Elysium. It was once home to {nickname} and Berenica, who lived there far removed from the world.

Long ago, the Elysians built a grand temple on the island, dedicated to the Goddess of the Full Moon and Fate. The structure was partially destroyed during the Great Migration nearly a millennium ago, after which the island faded into obscurity.

A century ago, a group of Imperial fishermen — fleeing heavy taxation — arrived in secret. They chose to stay, eventually settling and founding the quiet village that still exists today.
One of the Hyperborean Empire's provinces, located at the northernmost edge of the Empire's territory. Approximately half its landmass is occupied by the Vidofnir Mountains.

The largest city in northern Hyperborea. Situated south of the Vidofnir Mountains, it falls under the jurisdiction of Cocytus Province. The city takes its name from the nearby Lamenting Lake, which remains frozen for most of the year due to the harsh climate. Only during the three-month-long "Thawing Season" does the ice begin to melt.

Founded during the Great Migration by Dis I, the Empire's first sovereign, Icelake was among the earliest cities established in Hyperborea. For centuries, it served as a fortress city guarding the Empire's northern border.

Roughly 150 years ago, Icelake flourished during a boom in alchemical research and the advancement of Phoxichor technology. The nearby Heaventree enriched local Phoxichor veins, fuelling rapid industrial development and urban expansion. Today, with the veins nearly exhausted, that prosperity has faded, and the once-vibrant industry is now in decline.

The city is divided into the inner city and four surrounding districts.

The inner city, also known as the Old Quarter, houses the Council Hall, the Alchemy Academy, and military headquarters. Access and residency are tightly restricted: only nobles, senior officials, wealthy merchants, and those in their service are permitted to enter.

The city's slums are commonly referred to as Mist Aken — a term in the local dialect meaning "the Mist District." Located near the exhaust vents of Icelake's core infrastructure, the area is perpetually shrouded in haze due to constant emissions of waste gases. While the environment poses significant health risks, the slightly higher temperatures caused by the fumes have ironically made Mist Aken a haven for physically frail or cold-sensitive Charon residents. Despite poor law enforcement, the district's relative lack of Solarian authority has, in some respects, made it the safest place in Icelake for the Charon underclass.

The city's sewer network is vast and labyrinthine, with numerous sections repurposed into military facilities by the Aeolipile. The purpose and function of many of these installations remain classified.
The capital of the Hyperborean Empire.
The southernmost province of the Hyperborean Empire, bordering both the Elysian Church and Aethyrie, the Free State.
A major city in the southern reaches of the Empire, under the jurisdiction of Flagson Province.
A strategic stronghold of the Hyperborean Empire, situated on the highlands above Agate Valley. Once seized by The Forsakens, it was later reclaimed by Imperial forces in a military operation.
One of the most prosperous streets in the imperial capital, Dismania. Lined with the city's finest restaurants and entertainment venues, its lights shine brightly late into the night.

A river that flows through the heart of Dismania. Once a key transport waterway, it has since become a beloved scenic landmark. During the rainy season, the soft patter of raindrops on its surface is said to resemble gentle whispers — a quality that inspired its poetic name.

A nation in the far east of the Atlasia Continent, united by its reverence for "Heaven". Its entire territory is governed by the supreme natural law known as the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, and the Lord Argent, Taihao, is revered as the living embodiment of this law. Here, incense serves as the primary medium through which people communicate with Taihao.
Huaxu is a realm committed to coexistence and peace, standing in stark contrast to the Hyperborean Empire.
Huaxu is renowned as the "Realm of Peace." Within its borders, any act of direct physical harm against another person is strictly forbidden.

A major port in southern Huaxu where rivers meet the sea. Located near the old capital Haojing, it's known for its mild climate and scenic views. This trading hub serves as the main entry point for foreigners visiting Huaxu.

Mistwharf's black market, located on its western shore — a ship graveyard bordering Gritblight Expanse.
Ambitious Huaxu fishermen seeking quick wealth through smuggling depart from here, braving treacherous covert routes to other regions. Hidden currents often wreck their vessels, washing the wreckage ashore. Over time, this created the graveyard.
The area's natural concealment and isolation attracted opportunistic merchants, forming a grey-market bazaar.

The dwelling of Wishen, the Spring of Yu is a central lake isle in Mistwharf, cited in antiquity as "the liminal crossing of this world and the next." Entry requires the personal invitation of a Wishen.

The ancient battlefield of the Battle of Shuli, located northwest of Mistwharf as a solitary island surrounded by sea. 
It was once a key research site for Jishu Sect, and though most constructs were destroyed in the war, some remain fully functional, defending against intruders and deterring visitors. This deserted area later became a haven for birds, particularly crows, whose persistent presence gave the place its name.
An altar erected by predecessors to seal Zhuyin, standing amidst turbulent seas and facing the Gritblight Expanse from afar. Zhiliu plans to achieve Zhuyin's re-sealing in this place.

The historic capital of Huaxu, with a history stretching back more than a thousand years to the founding of the nation. Crowning the city's highest point is the Hall of Adjudication, an imposing edifice that symbolises the authority of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.

The Port of Parting Stars takes its name from an old proverb: "When the parting stars meet, merchants flock in." It is the largest harbour in Haojing and the region's primary centre of trade, with merchant vessels coming and going in an endless stream.

Said to lie hidden among mountains veiled in cloud, Outer Peaks is difficult to find, yet that very seclusion makes it an ideal refuge for those who seek to oppose the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. It serves as the Drifters' secret stronghold.

An underground palace built by the Jishu Sect during its ancient heyday. Rumour has it that deep within lies a relic left behind by the Sect's forebears, one powerful enough to turn the tide of battle. Yet its defensive mechanisms are so intricate that, to this day, no one has reached its depths.
A quiet, idyllic village on the outskirts of Haojing, famed for its incense-making.

The Taixu Mausoleum, suspended within the dome high above the Hall of Adjudication, forms the heart of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. Throughout history, many High Chancellors of Loongyuan have sacrificed themselves here, giving their lives to sustain the Nine Chapters.

A major railway station in Icelake's inner city, formally known as Flodia Bloomfield Station. It was named after Princess Flodia, the eldest daughter of the previous Emperor, whose birth coincided with the station's completion.

The station currently has seven tracks and eight platforms, making it a key transport hub for Cocytus. A vast ironworks complex lies beneath it and continues to expand to this day.

A mountain in the southern mountain range of Flagson. Four years ago, the war between Hyperborea and Elysian Church reached the area around Mount Arcano. Since then, human presence in the mountains has become scarce.

The war four years ago left an irreversible mark on Mount Arcano. The town of Arcano was destroyed, its villagers all perished, and large areas became uninhabitable. In addition, retreating Elysian Church soldiers laid extensive landmines across the area to slow the Empire's pursuit. These factors combined have kept the Empire from reclaiming or rebuilding Mount Arcano and the town of Arcano over the years.

The town of Arcano is a mountain settlement on a plateau in southern Flagson, sharing the mountain's name. It started as a small settlement, but after the villagers built an amusement park within the town, a surge of tourists flooded in. The town expanded and became a thriving tourist destination.
During the war four years ago, the town of Arcano briefly served as one of the many supply stops for the border legions. But as the conflict intensified, many once-safe towns were drawn into the flames of war — and Arcano was among those that fell.
Mother Bunny single-handedly rebuilt Arcano amidst the war-torn ruins of Mount Arcano, renaming it Paradise Village. Survivors now live peaceful, content lives here.
Paradise Village has a set of rules that everyone must follow. According to the villagers, it is these rules that restored peace to the village after the chaos of war.

Most of the original residents of Arcano died in the war. The current residents of Paradise Village are outsiders who were coerced by the village chief and Mother Bunny into playing the roles of the deceased. Those who break the rules or fail to perform their roles are executed by the chief and buried in the cemetery beneath the Pond of Slumber.

"Till the day we meet again."

Written by Aura

{nickname} grew up with Berenica on Purgatorio Island, a small isle between Hyperborea and Elysium.

One day, a Filthoid horde tore their peaceful lives apart. Desperate to escape, {nickname} and Berenica fled to the ruins of an ancient shrine.

But an unexpected visitor was already waiting for them there. From that moment on, their lives would never be the same...

"Flowers bring good luck."

Written by Aura

Separated from Berenica and cast into the sea, {nickname} was rescued by a mysterious figure in white and taken to Icelake, a city in northern Hyperborea.

Everything about Icelake felt strange, as though nothing quite added up. Yet Psyche, a receptionist at Hypnos' House, offered a rare warmth in this frozen land.

To survive — and to keep searching for Berenica — {nickname} joined forces with Outsider, a Phoxhunter, and Snow, a Lunarian. Together, they formed a team known as the Noctoyagers, while {nickname} took on a new identity as a Phoxhunter.

At the same time, a shadowy conspiracy surrounding Hypnos' House began to emerge. Every lead pointed towards the cursed ancient bloodline of the Charon...

"May the nameless child be bathed in pure light."

Written by Aura and AYIN

In the dead of night, a grotesque creature stalked the streets of Icelake.

Seeking the truth behind the tragedy known as the Charon Hunt, the Noctoyagers accepted a request from Rhythm, a junior officer in the Icelake Escort.

The creature's identity remained a mystery. All signs pointed to the Forsakens, but the sudden involvement of the 13th Legion only made the case harder to untangle.

Just as Rhythm and the Noctoyagers reached a dead end, the creature came to them of its own accord, bringing with it a truth both tragic and terrifying...

"You who claim innocence — if your resolve still holds true, then forge that will into a blade... and answer me with your sword!"

Written by Aura

This tale comes from the far side of the Sandrealm.

During the 13th Legion's campaign to retake Lonza Fortress, {nickname2} and Daphne, the squad's medic, were drawn into a desperate battle.

Their plan of attack had been leaked. The Forsakens were already lying in ambush, turning the fortress into a merciless killing ground for the Legion. No reinforcements came. There was a mole in their ranks. The mission was plagued by one mishap after another. Even the young girl they had rescued seemed to be hiding something...

With the last of their strength, {nickname2} and their commanding officer, Avar, fought their way to the heart of the fortress, only to discover that all the bloodshed may have been nothing more than a game orchestrated by the Overlookers above...

"No matter how dark or scary the world might seem... as long as she held hands with her friends, she could always find her way to a rainbow-coloured dream."

Written by Beryl

Fina has long remained shut away at home, her frail health and the need to stay hidden from trouble keeping her apart from the outside world. She has grown used to pouring her imagination into ink, filling the pages of her notebook with vast worlds of her own. Even so, she has never stopped yearning for the world beyond her door.

Then, encouraged by Outsider and {nickname}, she finally finds the courage to step outside and explore Icelake — a city as beautiful as it is cruel.

As she meets new people and makes friends along the way, Fina uses her magic and her quill to bring one whimsical companion after another to life, helping those in need and resolving the troubles she encounters. But when someone from her past appears without warning, she is forced to confront the memories she has kept buried for so long...

"The age of the Lord Argent Sovereign ends here. And I shall claim Their mantle."
